_note: Core English dictionary for the understanding module (memory/researcher/understanding.py). Format: term -> [definition, usage]. Definitions <=12 words. Sibling: dictionary_project.json. Pointer: memory/INDEX.md.

memory.definition: stored information kept for later use
memory.usage: the agent keeps project memory in files

recall.definition: bring stored information back into mind or context
recall.usage: recall the last decision before answering

remember.definition: keep something in mind; store for later
remember.usage: remember to commit after each change

context.definition: surrounding information that gives meaning to a request

prompt.definition: the user's current instruction to the model
prompt.usage: extract key terms from every prompt

reply.definition: a response given back to the asker
reply.usage: post the reply, then run recall

model.definition: an AI system that processes text and predicts
model.usage: pick a smaller model for background tasks

agent.definition: a program that acts on behalf of a user
agent.usage: the agent reads memory before acting

module.definition: a self-contained unit of code in one file
module.usage: import the understanding module at startup

function.definition: a named block of code that takes inputs and returns output
function.usage: call the lookup function with the term

variable.definition: a named value that can change during a run
variable.usage: store the result in a variable

loop.definition: repeating a set of steps until a condition ends it
loop.usage: loop over each key term in turn

error.definition: something going wrong; a failure signal from code
error.usage: log the error and degrade gracefully

bug.definition: an unintended flaw in code causing wrong behavior

test.definition: a check that verifies code behaves as expected
test.usage: run the test suite after each patch

commit.definition: save a snapshot of changes into version control
commit.usage: commit the dictionary files with a short message

branch.definition: a parallel line of development in a repo
branch.usage: work on a branch, then merge

merge.definition: combine two lines of development into one
merge.usage: merge the feature once tests pass

patch.definition: a small set of changes applied to existing code
patch.usage: apply the patch script, check its markers

anchor.definition: an exact text snippet used to locate a change point
anchor.usage: splice new code before the anchor line

index.definition: a lookup structure mapping keys to locations or values
index.usage: build an index of memory files by term

pointer.definition: a reference that says where something else lives
pointer.usage: INDEX.md holds pointers to every memory module

file.definition: a named block of data stored on disk
file.usage: write the result to a json file

folder.usage: keep researcher notes in one folder

path.definition: the address of a file or folder on disk
path.usage: use relative paths from the project root

line.definition: one row of text in a file
line.usage: replace only the target line, not neighbors

code.definition: instructions written for a computer to execute
code.usage: read the code before changing it

script.definition: a short program run directly, often one-off
script.usage: run the patch script from the terminal

execute.definition: run code so its instructions take effect
execute.usage: execute the tool call in order

build.definition: assemble or create something from parts
build.usage: build pre-context before sending the prompt

fix.definition: repair something that is broken or wrong

verify.definition: check that something is true or correct
verify.usage: verify the file exists before reading it

confirm.definition: state that something has been checked and is so
confirm.usage: confirm the test passed before moving on

check.definition: look at something to see if it is right

log.definition: a running record of events, written in order
log.usage: append each step to the run log

state.definition: the current condition or values of a system
state.usage: read the goal state from the ledger

status.definition: a short report on how something is going
status.usage: post status only when it changes

goal.definition: a desired outcome the work is aimed at
goal.usage: keep main goals moving without holdups

task.definition: a unit of work to be done
task.usage: queue the task in the background list

queue.definition: an ordered list of items waiting for processing
queue.usage: long probes go to the background queue

blocker.definition: something that prevents progress until resolved
blocker.usage: list every blocker, then clear them one by one

stall.definition: progress stopping even though work should continue
stall.usage: a stalled goal needs a nudge or re-plan

change.usage: record each change with a commit

update.usage: update the index after adding files

add.definition: include something that was not there before
add.usage: add the new term to the dictionary

remove.definition: take something out so it is no longer present
remove.usage: remove stale entries from the log

delete.usage: delete only after a backup exists

create.definition: make something that did not exist before
create.usage: create the data file with sample entries

write.definition: produce text or data into a file or field
write.usage: write results as json, one record per line

read.definition: take in text or data to use it
read.usage: read the last twenty prompts for gaps

send.definition: transmit something from here to somewhere else
send.usage: send the pre-context with the main prompt

receive.usage: receive the tool result before continuing

message.definition: a unit of communication between people or systems
message.usage: each chat message becomes one agent turn

chat.definition: an ongoing conversation, here between user and agents

user.definition: the person giving instructions and receiving results
user.usage: ask the user before buying or deleting

tool.definition: a capability an agent can call to act
tool.usage: use a tool when it materially improves the answer

call.definition: one use of a function or tool with its arguments
call.usage: batch independent calls into one block

result.definition: the output produced by running something
result.usage: keep results minimal to save context

output.definition: what a program or model produces
output.usage: cap the output length for long files

input.definition: what is given to a program or model to process
input.usage: clean the input before keying terms

data.definition: facts and values stored for later processing
data.usage: load the data file once at startup

record.definition: one entry in a structured collection of entries
record.usage: append one record per completed task

note.definition: a short written reminder or observation
note.usage: leave a note explaining the decision

plan.definition: an ordered set of steps toward a goal
plan.usage: work the plan in small parts

step.definition: one action within a larger sequence
step.usage: take one step, then check the screen

limit.definition: the maximum allowed amount of something

budget.definition: an allowance of a resource, here tokens or time
budget.usage: spend the output budget on code, not prose

token.definition: one unit of text a model counts against its budget
token.usage: shorter replies leave more tokens for tools
